title: Emrys and the Orbit
premise: Bram Halloran wakes into a life they never lived: the memories, debts, and unfinished murder investigation of the original Bram Halloran, killed before his clone decanted. On Meridian Station, a dying orbital colony the corporation has quietly written off, Bram discovers the original was investigating a massacre aboard the ship Perihelion—a vessel that officially never flew. As life support fails and colonists are 'relocated' one by one, Bram finds a name on a manifest that shouldn't exist: their own. To survive, Bram must expose the truth hidden in the station's bones, ally with the last engineer who remembers, and confront the corporate heir whose inheritance depends on the massacre staying buried—ending with Bram broadcasting the proof as the station falls, choosing memory over survival.
about_author: Ines Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing ships that were decommissioned, renamed, or erased from registries entirely. They write science fiction about records, rot, and the people history tries to lose.

chapters.title: Decant Day
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Waking in a cloning facility on Meridian Station with another person's memories settling like sediment, Bram learns the original died three weeks ago—an 'accident' no one will discuss. The emotional beat is disorientation curdling into quiet anger: this life was handed to them secondhand, murder included.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sorting the original's quarters, Bram finds a hidden cache: notes on the Perihelion, a colony ship that official logs say never launched, and forty-one names crossed out in red. The station's doctor warns them to stop asking questions. Beat: dread mixed with obligation—the dead man's work now belongs to them.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, shifting to engineer Sefa Okonkwo's voice mid-chapter. Cross-referencing power-grid anomalies with cargo records, Bram confirms the Perihelion docked here eleven years ago—and left with fewer souls than it carried. Sefa, the only crew member still stationed, recognizes the handwriting. Beat: the first thrill of corroboration, shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: Relocation
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Corporate shuttles begin removing colonists 'for their safety' as oxygen recyclers fail on schedule. Sefa realizes the station isn't dying—it's being euthanized, and the timeline matches the original Bram's investigation. Beat: helplessness hardening into resolve; the massacre may not be finished.

chapters.title: A Name That Shouldn't Be There
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Deep in the archive vault, Bram finds the Perihelion's true manifest—and their own name, dated before their decant. The original knew he'd be cloned; he hid evidence inside his own genetic line. Beat: vertigo. Bram isn't just inheriting the case—they were designed as its courier.

chapters.title: The Heir
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Bram and Adrien Voss, corporate scion overseeing the station's closure. Voss offers Bram a transfer, wealth, erasure of their clone status—if they hand over the original's files. His charm frays into threat. Beat: temptation and the first clear sight of the enemy, who is killing the station to bury a decade-old crime.

chapters.title: What the Hull Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa and Bram's shared POV. Following the original's clues into the sealed lower decks, they find the Perihelion itself—never flown away, just re-registered—and inside, the physical evidence: scorch patterns, sealed compartments, forty-one sets of remains the company logged as 'cargo loss.' Beat: horror made tangible; grief for strangers who were someone's family.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Voss accelerates the demolition schedule; security sweeps the station. Sefa is detained, and Bram learns their own termination order is already signed—the clone was always disposable. Racing through failing corridors, Bram retrieves the data core from the wreck. Beat: pure momentum, terror sharpened by purpose.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax. From the station's ancient comm array, Bram transmits the full record—manifests, hull footage, the forty-one names—to every relay in the system as Voss's team breaches the array room. Confrontation at gunpoint; Voss hesitates because the broadcast can't be stopped, only outlived. Beat: defiant clarity—truth as the only inheritance worth keeping.

chapters.title: Orbit
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue tone. Meridian falls silent; Bram evacuates on the last shuttle alongside freed Sefa and the final colonists, watching the station burn up on reentry like a funeral pyre. Months later, hearings begin, Voss is indicted, and Bram—still legally no one—adds their own name beneath the forty-one. Beat: mourning transformed into witness; survival as testimony.
